programme_target.summary: For every Leray-Hopf solution generated by smooth divergence-free rapidly decaying data on R3, the critical integral of the fourth power of the L6 norm is finite on every finite time interval.

status_authority.statement: MATH-PROGRAMME retains target, status, and promotion authority. The upstream Clay statement is a formulation source, not the NS-CI campaign definition.

findings.summary: The upstream theorem formalizes Clay alternative A for global smooth existence on R3 with positive viscosity and zero forcing.
NS-CI-001 is not the upstream theorem: it quantifies over Leray-Hopf solutions and asserts a critical spacetime integrability condition.
The admitted relationship is only the Programme-target-to-Clay-A sufficiency direction; no reverse implication is promoted.
The upstream Lean file cannot certify the critical-integral route because its open theorem ends with sorry and does not state the Serrin continuation implication.

obligations: Retain the Leray-Hopf solution class, data assumptions, time horizon, and L4_t L6_x integral exactly in all NS-CI handoffs.
Prove or source-audit the one-way continuation implication before any theorem-level promotion.
Do not infer the NS-CI target from the existence of an upstream Lean declaration or from successful elaboration with sorry.
Do not promote the reverse implication from Clay alternative A to universal critical integrability.
claim_boundary: This concordance records a one-way route relationship only. It does not prove critical integrability, global regularity, equivalence with Clay alternative A, or correctness of the upstream open theorem.
